title: Two Work Packages write the same two story files and the same two fragments for legacy RWB-AD-012 on rwb-access
source: Work Package files _work/msr/wp/B-P4-04.md (its Write only block lists the two AD012 story files at lines 16-17 and the two fragments at lines 26-27) and _work/msr/wp/B2-P4-006.md (the same four paths at lines 9-12); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (exactly two slices for legacy RWB-AD-012: RWB-P4-AD012-CON in lane CG-W4 Day 1 and RWB-P4-AD012-APP in lane L-P4-G ready after RWB-P4-AD011-APP, both wave 4, both release 30 June 2027, both disposition Split (rework)); _work/msr/status.json (no key for B-P4-04 and no key for B2-P4-006); _work/msr/editlog (no B-P4-04.md, so the delivered files have no edit log of their own); _work/msr/gaps/B-P4-04.jsonl and _work/msr/assumptions/B-P4-04.jsonl (the citation set the four delivered artefacts carry)
section: Whole file set of RWB-AD-012 on rwb-access: the two story files and the fragments _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P4-AD012-APP.json and RWB-P4-AD012-CON.json
description: The plan carries two slices for legacy RWB-AD-012 on rwb-access (a contract baseline and an application slice), but two Work Packages of the run name them: B-P4-04, which lists RWB-AD-012 beside RWB-AD-013 inside a fanout, and B2-P4-006, which names the same two story files and the same two fragments alone with fanout 0. The four artefacts are present and complete in the tree: the two story files are 66,617 and 37,452 bytes, each with the two header lines of Template and Rules v1 R8.1, a D-RCV-60 change-log row carrying the tool line T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash, the 20 metadata rows of R7.1 in order, the 19 section headings in order, tables 12.1 to 12.9, the R7.2 Level column in section 16 and no as-built heading because neither slice is preserved; the app file carries AC1 and AC2 of RWB-AD-012 word for word with their origin tags plus one mock Given line, and the contract file carries six criteria tagged as new under D-RCV-60. Both fragments parse and carry the 28 keys WP item 8 lists, and every CG and ASM id the artefacts cite resolves to a row of gaps/B-P4-04.jsonl or assumptions/B-P4-04.jsonl. The only difference from a fresh execution of B2-P4-006 is the citation family: the delivered set is CG-B-P4-04-AD012-101 to -107 and ASM-B-P4-04-AD012-101 to -107.
evidence: wp/B-P4-04.md lines 16-17 and 26-27 against wp/B2-P4-006.md lines 9-12 name the identical four output paths; split_plan.json carries exactly two slices for RWB-AD-012 and both Work Packages name them; status.json has 156 keys and none is B-P4-04 or B2-P4-006; editlog holds B-P4-01, -03, -05, -06, -07, -08, -09, -10, -12, -13 and -14 and no B-P4-04; gaps/B-P4-04.jsonl holds 7 rows (CG-B-P4-04-AD012-101 to -107) and assumptions/B-P4-04.jsonl holds 7 rows; measured sizes 66,617 and 37,452 bytes for the two story files and 3,105 and 2,886 bytes for the two fragments
proposed: Keep one Work Package per story slice in the plan generator: remove RWB-AD-012 from the B-P4-04 fanout list, or retire B2-P4-006 for this key. At step D1, number CG-B-P4-04-AD012-101 to -107 and ASM-B-P4-04-AD012-101 to -107 once and allocate no second set for B2-P4-006. Ask the B-P4-04 execution to write its edit log row so the delivered AD012 citation set has a traceable writer, and add a plan-uniqueness check to checks/run_all.py that fails when two Work Package Write only blocks name the same output path.
